title: Reading Drill — Packing Fruit for a Long Journey
description: One short passage, five questions. Recommended time: 8 minutes.

passages.title: Packing Fruit for a Long Journey
passages.body:
**A** A distributor noticed that pears were bruised most often near the corners of large trays. Workers added a thin divider to prevent the fruit from rolling into those spaces.

**B** The dividers reduced bruising but made the trays slower to fill. The supervisor tested whether smaller trays could obtain similar results without an extra assembly step.

**C** The evaluation included a cost for handling damaged fruit. It also noted that loose pears usually left customers with more control over portion size.

questions.prompt: Workers added a thin ______ to prevent the fruit from rolling into those spaces.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: Workers added a thin divider to prevent the fruit from rolling into those spaces.

questions.prompt: The supervisor tested whether ______ could obtain similar results without an extra assembly step.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: The supervisor tested whether smaller trays could obtain similar results without an extra assembly step.

questions.prompt: It also noted that loose pears usually left customers with more control over ______.
questions.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage.
questions.explanation: It also noted that loose pears usually left customers with more control over portion size.

questions.prompt: The shipment travelled by rail for part of the journey.
questions.instructions: Does this statement agree with the information in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage does not state this information.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph mentions one disadvantage caused by the initial solution?
questions.explanation: The dividers reduced bruising but made the trays slower to fill. The supervisor tested whether smaller trays could obtain similar results without an extra assembly step.
